scheduler_signal.summary: A closed, finite model-counterfactual intent is ready for independent domain realization review. It jointly tests the reviewed constant-surface-boundary and tail-support-artifact hypotheses using four primary one-dimensional material/boundary cells plus tightened reruns, with both mandatory profiles, their gaps, shared support, and the approximate SIMS limit preserved. No experiment results or result analysis were supplied, so no mechanism is selected. The bound execution context identifies SProcess R-2020.09 but declares no capability statements or limitations; the historical initialized project concerns a different objective and candidate set and is not execution qualification for this intent.

payload.priority_rationale: This is the first and only current proposal because the same four finite solver cells test whether the two supplied Table I surface anchors causally control the material contrast, while the same raw outputs support a no-cost detection-limit and shared-support sensitivity. It precedes the higher-flexibility continuous-response and two-regime comparisons: if the observable contrast is dominated by the boundary anchors or disappears after admissibility filtering, extra bulk-law degrees of freedom are not yet identifiable. The historical project reached materialization, preflight, and initialization for an older reproduction plan, showing progress toward a one-dimensional SProcess workflow, but its old hypothesis keys, grids, numerical settings, and qualification are not reused. No new results or analysis were supplied.

cases.purpose: In0.83Al0.17As with D_Al and Cs=6.85 x 10^19 cm^-3; supplies the Al own-anchor cell and the Al member of the common-low comparison.
In0.83Al0.17As with unchanged D_Al and Cs changed only to 8.35 x 10^19 cm^-3; supplies the Al member of the common-high comparison.
In0.83Ga0.17As with D_Ga and Cs=8.35 x 10^19 cm^-3; supplies the Ga own-anchor cell and the Ga member of the common-high comparison.
In0.83Ga0.17As with unchanged D_Ga and Cs changed only to 6.85 x 10^19 cm^-3; supplies the Ga member of the common-low comparison.

Rerun all four primary cells with maximum spatial and time steps halved and L increased by 50%; do not refit or change any physical input. Use paired predictions to compute u_num and confirm decision stability.

current_objectives: Determine whether changing only the constant effective surface concentration between the two exact Table I anchors accounts for at least half of the supported material contrast while holding the material-specific constant-D anchor, thermal history, equation, initial condition, and reduction fixed.

Determine whether the apparent qualified tail and material contrast change materially when rows at or below 3 x 10^15 cm^-3 and shared-support rows are handled by the preregistered admissibility and weighting rules.
frozen_invariants: Use both mandatory observables from objective.fig4_mechanism_discrimination: the two legend-bound Zn concentration-depth profiles and their supported front/tail contrast. Never use the paper fit overlay as observations or infer behavior across the 235-pixel InAlAs gap.
Temperature is exactly 480 degrees C and elapsed diffusion time is exactly 480 s in every physical case; no other temperature, time, layer stack, source history, or device process is introduced.

For material m, solve the bounded phenomenological family partial C_m/partial t = D_m partial^2 C_m/partial x^2 for 0<x<L and 0<t<=480 s, with C_m(x,0)=0, C_m(0,t)=Cs, and C_m(L,t)=0. Use D_Al=1.59 x 10^-12 cm^2/s and D_Ga=1.05 x 10^-12 cm^2/s only as the supplied Table I comparison anchors.

Set L deterministically to x_max + 6 sqrt(D_max t), where x_max is the deepest existing supplied target depth, D_max=1.59 x 10^-12 cm^2/s, and t=480 s. This fixes the remote boundary from declared inputs without fitting it; report L in the case ledger.

The only physical intervention is Cs at one of the two exact supplied anchors: 6.85 x 10^19 or 8.35 x 10^19 cm^-3. The complete 2 material x 2 boundary factorial is evaluated; no interpolation, optimization, widening, time-dependent source, extra channel, fitted exponent, or defect identity is allowed.

Primary evidence comprises existing direct-pixel rows with observed central concentration strictly above 3 x 10^15 cm^-3. Rows at or below that approximate SIMS limit are sensitivity-only. Rows sharing one source pixel or explicit provenance identifier form one dependence group and receive total group weight one.

Preserve every existing point index, series identity, concentration/depth bound, gap, and support label. Sample simulated log10 concentration only at existing target depths by monotone interpolation on the solver mesh; never create a target row or bridge a missing interval.

For row i use y_i=log10(C_i/cm^-3), residual r_i=yhat_i-y_i, concentration half-width u_C,i equal to the larger supplied log bound, and u_i^2=u_C,i^2+(abs(dyhat/dx)u_x,i)^2+u_num,i^2. The tightened rerun supplies u_num,i=abs(yhat_tight,i-yhat_primary,i).

For set A compute WRMSE_log=sqrt(sum(w_i r_i^2)/sum(w_i)), Q=sum(w_i(r_i/u_i)^2), weighted in-band fraction=sum(w_i I(abs(r_i)<=u_i))/sum(w_i), and effective count equal to the number of dependence groups. Report all metrics separately by material, primary/tail segment, and sensitivity mask.

Define front depth as the monotone crossing of 5.4 x 10^16 cm^-3 within existing supported depth span, and qualified dose as the trapezoidal integral only over contiguous primary intervals. If a crossing is absent or a gap separates required bracketing rows, mark it missing rather than extrapolating.

A boundary contrast statistic is the Euclidean norm of standardized between-material differences in front depth and log10 qualified dose. Compute it for own anchors, common low anchor, and common high anchor. Boundary-collapse fraction is R=1-max(Delta_common_low,Delta_common_high)/Delta_own; uncertainty bounds use first-order propagation from row bounds and u_num with shared groups counted once.

No output from this study establishes kick-out, VCD, or another microscopic mechanism. The two-regime and continuous-response hypotheses remain deferred until the present boundary and evidence-support gates are resolved.

ambiguity_conditions: The 95% interval for R crosses 0.25 or 0.50.
Either common-boundary front crossing is absent within supported rows or requires bridging the InAlAs gap.
The primary tail contains fewer than five independent direct-pixel groups in either material.
A decision changes under the declared numerical, shared-support, or detection-limit sensitivity.
identifiability_claims.decision_rule: Apply the surface-control 0.50/0.25 gates only after numerical checks and both per-material adequacy checks pass; then apply the artifact 50%/10% sensitivity gates. Never select a microscopic mechanism from either outcome.
identifiability_claims.distinguishing_outcome: A stable R>=0.50 after admissibility filtering attributes most observable contrast to the bounded boundary intervention; a large mask dependence instead shows that the tail cannot securely discriminate the physical boundary response.
identifiability_claims.observable: Factorial boundary-collapse fraction and its stability to support/limit masks.
identifiability_claims.smallest_resolving_control: Obtain independently qualified author raw SIMS values with row-level detection status and uncertainty for the same samples, or, for numerical ambiguity only, repeat the exact four cells at the registered tightened resolution without changing physics.

ambiguity_conditions: Any required support identifier, concentration/depth bound, or detection-limit provenance is absent.
Sensitivity changes are greater than 10% but less than 50%.
Either material has fewer than five direct-pixel primary dependence groups in the tail segment.
The effect depends on bridging the 235-pixel InAlAs gap or on a changed numerical result.
identifiability_claims.decision_rule: Use the fixed 50% support, 10% rejection, and intermediate inconclusive gates only after exact evidence-mask fidelity and numerical convergence pass; treat below-limit and shared-inclusive variants as sensitivities that cannot create a physical-mechanism preference.
identifiability_claims.distinguishing_outcome: A change of at least 50% or a changed boundary category identifies evidence support as decision-limiting; changes no greater than 10% with stable propagated intervals reject the bounded artifact explanation for the supported tail.
identifiability_claims.observable: Change in tail extent, standardized material contrast, and boundary decision category across direct-pixel primary, shared-group, shared-inclusive, and sub-limit-inclusive reductions.
identifiability_claims.smallest_resolving_control: Obtain independently qualified author raw SIMS values for the same 480 degrees C, 8 min samples with row-level measurement-limit status, uncertainties, and unambiguous material identity.

objectives: Use the supplied paper evidence to support later selection of falsifiable hypotheses and design of a minimal TCAD control experiment, while this Intake is limited to evidence extraction and does not select a hypothesis.

Determine whether changing only the constant effective surface concentration between the two exact Table I anchors accounts for at least half of the supported material contrast while holding the material-specific constant-D anchor, thermal history, equation, initial condition, and reduction fixed.

Determine whether the apparent qualified tail and material contrast change materially when rows at or below 3 x 10^15 cm^-3 and shared-support rows are handled by the preregistered admissibility and weighting rules.

If boundary control is rejected or remains ambiguous and the above-limit direct-pixel tail remains stable, later compare the reviewed continuous material response with the reviewed two-regime kick-out/VCD phenomenology using a separately reviewed finite model family.

prediction_tests.expected_result: Both common-boundary comparisons reduce the standardized material contrast so that the lower 95% bound of R is at least 0.50, each material's own-anchor WRMSE_log is at most 0.15 decade, and changing Cs moves dose and front depth coherently in both materials.
prediction_tests.falsifying_result: Reject the bounded surface-control hypothesis if the upper 95% bound of R is at most 0.25, or if either material's own-anchor case fails WRMSE_log <=0.15 decade, or if the Cs intervention moves dose/front in opposite directions between materials after numerical checks pass. Values between the 0.25 and 0.50 gates are inconclusive.
prediction_tests.observable: Boundary-collapse fraction R from own-anchor versus common-low and common-high material contrasts, plus per-material whole-profile adequacy.

prediction_tests.expected_result: Support the evidence-artifact concern when admissibility changes reduce tail extent or material contrast by at least 50%, or change the boundary decision category; this limits mechanism claims but does not claim that the samples lack physical low-concentration Zn.
prediction_tests.falsifying_result: Reject the bounded artifact hypothesis when all admissibility variants change both tail extent and contrast by at most 10%, their propagated intervals remain separated from zero, and no decision category changes. Changes greater than 10% but less than 50% are inconclusive.
prediction_tests.observable: Relative change in supported tail extent and material-contrast statistic under primary direct-pixel, shared-group, shared-inclusive, and sub-limit-inclusive reductions.

required_observables: For every primary and tightened cell, the raw one-dimensional Zn concentration profile C(x,t=480 s), case identity, material identity, D, Cs, L, spatial/time controls, and solver termination state.

Predicted log10 concentration sampled at every existing target depth without filling missing point indices, together with supplied concentration/depth bounds, support class, shared group, primary/sub-limit mask, residual, propagated uncertainty, and numerical difference.
Per material and case: WRMSE_log, Q, weighted in-band fraction, effective group count, front crossing at 5.4 x 10^16 cm^-3 when supported, and qualified contiguous-interval dose.
Own-anchor, common-low, and common-high standardized material contrasts; boundary-collapse fraction R and propagated 95% interval.

Primary direct-pixel result, result after shared-group weighting, result including shared-support rows, and sensitivity-only result including rows at or below 3 x 10^15 cm^-3, with changes in tail extent, contrast, adequacy, and decision category.
Factorial boundary-collapse fraction and its stability to support/limit masks.
Change in tail extent, standardized material contrast, and boundary decision category across direct-pixel primary, shared-group, shared-inclusive, and sub-limit-inclusive reductions.
A complete finite case ledger showing four primary cells and four paired tightened reruns, with no fitted boundary history, extra channel, parameter widening, or cross-gap pseudo-observation.

resource_estimate.runtime_basis: Exactly four primary one-dimensional physical cells and four paired tightened reruns; all profile, boundary-collapse, uncertainty, shared-support, and detection-limit reductions reuse those eight raw outputs. Historical progress shows an older SProcess project was materialized and initialized, but the current execution context does not declare the capabilities needed for this new model, so resource feasibility remains conditional on a fresh domain review and initialization within the declared R-2020.09 backend.

stop_conditions: Stop before implementation if a registered Sentaurus R-2020.09 domain review cannot confirm the custom concentration state, equation, boundaries, clean case reset, or raw profile output; do not infer support from the backend name or historical qualification.
Stop if either mandatory profile, exact series identity, point indices, concentration/depth bounds, shared-support ownership, or detection-limit provenance required by reduction is unavailable.

Stop and report numerical inconclusive if any of the eight executions fails, produces a nonpositive or nonfinite primary prediction, omits an existing primary row, exceeds 0.05-decade paired convergence change, or changes the decision category when tightened.
Stop the physical comparison if either own-anchor material fails WRMSE_log <=0.15 decade; a contrast change from an inadequate base model cannot support boundary dominance.

Report surface boundary control rejected when the upper 95% bound of R is <=0.25, supported within this bounded phenomenology when the lower 95% bound is >=0.50 and all gates pass, and inconclusive otherwise.

Report tail support artifact supported when an admissibility variant changes tail extent or contrast by >=50% or changes the decision category, rejected when every change is <=10% with stable intervals, and inconclusive otherwise.

Stop as evidence-limited if a required front crossing or dose interval would bridge the InAlAs gap, depend on a row at or below 3 x 10^15 cm^-3, or leave fewer than five direct-pixel dependence groups in a claimed segment.
Do not add a surface-history parameter, optimize D or Cs, widen the two-anchor intervention, add a diffusion channel, or proceed to the deferred continuous/two-regime comparison in this experiment.
Stop after the finite factorial yields one supported, rejected, or inconclusive bounded disposition for each selected hypothesis; do not state a final microscopic mechanism.

value_assessment.rationale: Current coverage includes both original target observables through one four-cell surface-boundary factorial and a zero-solver-cost support/detection-limit sensitivity. The exact overall objective remains only partly closed because the experiment can accept or reject a bounded boundary explanation and judge tail admissibility, but cannot select kick-out/VCD or the continuous-response alternative. Those bulk-law objectives are deferred until boundary dominance is rejected or ambiguous and a stable above-limit direct-pixel tail remains; they then require a separately reviewed finite model family. Deferral does not undermine the validity of the present causal boundary contrast because material, D, time, equation, and reduction are fixed, but it limits claims to boundary-anchor sensitivity and evidence robustness. The design is minimal because the complete 2x2 material-by-anchor factorial is the smallest set that separates material and boundary effects, and its same outputs cover the artifact hypothesis. Evidence support is medium due to digitization, the InAlAs gap, shared pixels, and approximate detection limit. Feasibility is conditional because the execution context names SProcess R-2020.09 without declaring required capabilities, and the old initialized project is not inherited.

The two exact Table I anchors form the smallest finite causal boundary intervention with no fitted source history.
All supplied evidence is restricted to this temperature.
All supplied evidence is restricted to the 8 min treatment.
